'''Keti Tenenblat''' (born 27 November 1944) is a [[Turkish people|Turkish]]-[[Brazilians|Brazilian]] [[mathematician]] working on [[Riemannian geometry]], the applications of [[differential geometry]] to [[partial differential equations]], and [[Finsler geometry]]. Together with [[Chuu-Lian Terng]], she generalized Backlund theorem to higher dimensions.

== Education ==
Tenenblat was born on 27 November 1944  in [[İzmir]], Turkey, where she attended elementary and junior high school at an Italian school. In 1957, her family emigrated to Brazil. In Rio de Janeiro, she graduated from high school at Bennett College and joined the National Faculty of Philosophy at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro|University of Brazil]] (today UFRJ), in the Mathematics Degree.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.abc.org.br/membro/keti-tenenblat/|title=Keti Tenenblat|website=Academia Brasileira de Ciencias (Brazilian Academy of Sciences)|language=pt|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>

From 1964 to 1968, she taught mathematics at a secondary school in Rio. She completed her university course in 1967 and began her higher education activities at the Institute of Mathematics of [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro|UFRJ]] in 1968. Between 08/1968 to 07/1969, she attended a master's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]], USA, while accompanying her husband who was study abroad. Upon returning to Brazil, she returned to teaching at UFRJ and began a doctoral program at [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA]]. She defended her doctoral dissertation entitled "An estimate for the length of closed geodesics in Riemannian varieties" in 1972, under the direction of [[Manfredo do Carmo|Manfredo P. do Carmo]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
From 1973 she joined the faculty of the [[University of Brasília|University of Brasilia]] (UnB) where she became a Full Professor in 1989. From 1975 to 1978 she pursued a postdoctoral position at the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California]], Berkeley. During this period, she developed her research under the influence of [[Shiing-Shen Chern|S. S. Chern]] and became interested in studying the interaction between [[differential geometry]] and [[differential equation]]s.<ref name=":0" />

After 1978, her visits abroad were short-lived. She was a visiting professor at [[Yale University]], MSRI Berkeley, Institute of Theoretical Physics, Santa Barbara, IMA Minnesota, University of Montreal, McGill University, CRM Montreal, Nankai Institute and Fudan Univ. China.<ref name=":0" />

She is a recipient of [[National Order of Scientific Merit (Brazil)|Brazil's National Order of Scientific Merit]] in Mathematics,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mct.gov.br/index.php/content/view/11199/11199.html?nome=&area=Ci%EAncias+Matem%E1ticas&classificacao=&categoria=vivo|title=PORTAL DO MINISTÉRIO DA CIÊNCIA, TECNOLOGIA E INOVAÇÃO|work=Mct.gov.br|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150418134045/http://www.mct.gov.br/index.php/content/view/11199/11199.html?nome=&area=Ci%EAncias+Matem%E1ticas&classificacao=&categoria=vivo|archive-date=2015-04-18|accessdate=2015-05-28}}</ref> Emeritus Professor at the [[University of Brasília]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.secom.unb.br/unbagencia/ag1105-01.htm|title=SECOM - Secretaria de Comunicação da Universidade de Brasília (UnB)|work=Unb.br|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150418170650/http://www.secom.unb.br/unbagencia/ag1105-01.htm|archive-date=2015-04-18|accessdate=2015-05-28}}</ref> and was President of the [[Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática|Brazilian Mathematical Society]] in 1989–1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://matematicauniversitaria.ime.usp.br/Conteudo/n09_n10/n09_n10_Editorial.pdf|title=Elon Lages Lima|publisher=Matematicauniversitaria.ime.usp.br|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150418183012/http://matematicauniversitaria.ime.usp.br/Conteudo/n09_n10/n09_n10_Editorial.pdf|archive-date=2015-04-18|accessdate=2015-05-28}}</ref><ref>[http://www.sbm.org.br/institucional/quem-somos/memória/diretorias Brazilian Mathematical Society]</ref> She has been a member of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] since 1991.<ref name=":0"/>

She is also the author of the books ''{{lang|pt|Introdução à geometria diferencial}}'' (1988), and ''{{lang|pt|Transformações de superfícies e aplicações}}'' (1981).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mat.unb.br/keti/|title=Keti Tenenblat's Personal Webpage|website=Universidade de Brasília|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1965, she married Moyses Tenenblat, an engineer graduated from the National School of Engineering. Children Dany (1970), Nitza (1973), Leo (1975) and grandchildren Gabriel (1995), Yuri (1998), Luisa (2000), Clara (2005), Milla (2007), Aylou (2009), and Luca (2014) were born of this marriage.<ref name=":0" />
